title: Nevada Lawmaker Proposes Ban of Tech Behind Flock Safety Cameras

agency_candidates.display_name: Las Vegas Metro Police Department - NV

summary: Nevada Assemblymember Selena La Rue Hatch has submitted a bill draft request for the 2027 Legislature that would ban ALPR use in Nevada, going further than a separate interim committee proposal to regulate the technology. The article notes Las Vegas Metro operates 180 Flock cameras and 130 Motorola ALPRs, and includes reactions from the ACLU of Nevada, Flock, and FBI Director Kash Patel.

key_quotes.quote: The Northern Nevada Democrat submitted a bill draft request for the 2027 Legislature that — if signed into law — would ban the use of automated license plate readers and their associated networks
The Metropolitan Police Department has installed 180 Flock cameras across the jurisdiction, as well as 130 Motorola automated license plate reader cameras
This is the Silver State, not the Surveillance State, and I'm proud to sponsor this bill to ban Flock and ALPR surveillance networks.
